PHIN_REQ_001a: Systems designed to support OM must provide a [TBD: runtime/no-code or developer-assisted, release-based] configuration mechanism that allows an authorized administrator to add custom data fields to existing entities (e.g., health event records) without requiring a new software deployment. Acceptance criteria: (1) An administrator can create a new custom field via the configuration mechanism and have it available for data entry within [TBD: maximum propagation time, e.g., 5 minutes]; (2) New fields are automatically included in standard reporting outputs and data exports without additional code changes; (3) Attempting to create a field with a name that collides with an existing field name is rejected with a clear error message; (4) Deprecating or renaming a field preserves historical data integrity and does not break existing reports/exports referencing the prior field name.

PHIN_REQ_001b: Systems designed to support OM must provide a configuration mechanism that allows an authorized administrator to define new entity types and new relationship types between entities (e.g., to capture information unique to a particular health event type) via [TBD: runtime/no-code or developer-assisted, release-based] configuration. Relationship type definitions must specify cardinality (e.g., one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many) and referential integrity rules (e.g., [TBD: cascade delete, restrict, or orphan-handling policy]). Acceptance criteria: (1) An administrator can create a new entity type and a new relationship type and begin recording data against them within [TBD: maximum propagation time]; (2) The system enforces the defined cardinality and referential integrity rules, rejecting operations that would violate them; (3) Attempting to delete an entity type or relationship type that has existing referencing data is handled according to a defined policy (e.g., blocked, soft-deleted, or cascade-deleted per configuration), with the behavior clearly communicated to the administrator; (4) Newly defined entity types and relationship types can be mapped to standard vocabularies (e.g., LOINC, SNOMED) where applicable, and this mapping is validated at configuration time.

PHIN_REQ_001c: Systems designed to support OM must version all schema configuration changes (new fields, entity types, relationship types) and maintain backward compatibility for existing records created under prior schema versions. Acceptance criteria: (1) Each configuration change is recorded with a version identifier and timestamp; (2) Existing records created before a schema change remain valid, retrievable, and correctly displayed/exported after the change; (3) Downstream consumers (reports, APIs, exports) can identify which schema version applies to a given record; (4) Rolling back a configuration change does not corrupt or lose data captured under the newer schema version, following a defined [TBD: rollback/migration policy].

QHEADACHE_REQ_002 (Revised)

**Requirement:**
The product must track the active play session duration for the current user and display it in real time, so that [TBD: beneficiary — e.g., the player or a parent/guardian] can [TBD: purpose — e.g., monitor screen-time exposure as part of headache/eye-strain awareness tracking].

**Definitions:**
- "Play time" counts only active, foreground gameplay time within a single session; it excludes time while the app is paused, backgrounded, or the device is idle/locked.
- Tracking is per-session (resets to zero at the start of each new play session) unless [TBD: confirm whether cumulative/historical tracking across sessions is required].
- Timer precision: displayed in minutes:seconds (MM:SS), updated at least once per second, with accuracy tolerance of ±1 second over a 30-minute session.
- On backgrounding or pause, the timer must stop incrementing and resume accurately when the app returns to the foreground.
- On app crash or forced close, the session timer resets; partial session time is not persisted unless [TBD: confirm persistence requirement].
- The timer must remain accurate across device timezone changes, DST transitions, and manual system clock adjustments during an active session (based on elapsed monotonic time, not wall-clock time).

**Out of Scope:**
This requirement does not include: time limits, parental control restrictions, alerts/notifications, historical/cumulative charts across sessions, leaderboards, or multiplayer session aggregation. These are candidates for separate requirements.

**Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin):**

```
Scenario: Normal play session timer increments correctly
  Given the user starts a new play session
  When 65 seconds of active gameplay elapse
  Then the displayed play time shows "01:05" (±1 second tolerance)

Scenario: Timer pauses during backgrounding
  Given the user is in an active play session with displayed time "00:30"
  When the user backgrounds the app for 20 seconds and then returns
  Then the displayed play time resumes from "00:30" (±1 second tolerance)
  And the 20 seconds of background time is not counted

Scenario: Timer resets after app crash
  Given the user is in an active play session with displayed time "02:15"
  When the app crashes and is relaunched
  Then a new play session starts
  And the displayed play time begins at "00:00"
```

**Open items requiring PO confirmation:** beneficiary/purpose clause, cumulative vs. per-session tracking, persistence behavior on crash.

**SWPROJ_REQ_001a: Generate Random Coordinate Within Configurable Radius Annulus**

The system shall generate a random geographic coordinate (latitude/longitude, WGS84, decimal degrees, precision to [TBD: number of decimal places, e.g., 6]) located within an annulus around the user's current location, bounded by a minimum radius and a maximum radius.

- The minimum radius default shall be 2 km and the maximum radius default shall be 5 km; both values shall be configurable parameters (not hardcoded), with defaults documented and confirmed by stakeholders as either fixed business rules or tunable settings. [TBD: confirm with stakeholders whether 2–5 km is a hard constraint or configurable]
- The sampling method shall produce a point that is uniformly distributed over the **area** of the annulus (true area-uniform sampling), not uniform-radius sampling, to avoid center-clustering bias.
- The random number generator shall support an optional seed parameter to enable deterministic output for automated testing.
- Performance: coordinate generation shall complete within [TBD: maximum response time, e.g., 50 ms] per request under [TBD: expected load/concurrency].

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a user location and default radius bounds (2 km, 5 km), when a coordinate is generated, the haversine distance from the user's location to the generated coordinate shall be ≥ 2 km and ≤ 5 km (boundary values inclusive), within a rounding tolerance of [TBD: e.g., ±1 meter].
2. Given a sample of N = [TBD: e.g., 10,000] generated coordinates for a fixed user location, a chi-square (or equivalent) uniformity test over the annulus area shall confirm no statistically significant deviation from uniform-area distribution at a significance level of [TBD: e.g., 0.05].
3. Given the same seed value, repeated invocations shall produce identical coordinates, enabling deterministic regression tests.
4. The returned coordinate shall be valid WGS84 (latitude within [-90, 90], longitude within [-180, 180]) and formatted to the specified decimal precision.

**Out of Scope:** This requirement covers only coordinate math within the annulus. Location-permission handling, real-world validity filtering (e.g., land/water, restricted zones), and persistence/display of the generated coordinate are addressed in separate stories (see SWPROJ_REQ_001b and SWPROJ_REQ_001c).

---

**SWPROJ_REQ_001b: Real-World Validity Filtering of Generated Coordinates**

The system shall optionally filter generated coordinates (produced per SWPROJ_REQ_001a) to exclude points that fall on water, within restricted zones, or other invalid real-world locations, based on [TBD: data source/service for land/water and restricted-zone validation]. Acceptance criteria and retry/fallback behavior for rejected points are to be defined separately. [TBD: full scope and acceptance criteria]

---

**SWPROJ_REQ_001c: Location Permission Handling for Coordinate Generation**

The system shall request and verify the necessary device/user location permissions before invoking coordinate generation (per SWPROJ_REQ_001a), handling permission-denied and permission-revoked states per [TBD: platform-specific permission UX guidelines]. Acceptance criteria to be defined separately. [TBD: full scope and acceptance criteria]
